provenance.paper_title: AViLA: Asynchronous Vision-Language Agent for Streaming Multimodal Data Interaction

evidence.paraphrase: The memory retains historical streaming observations even when queries and evidence arrive asynchronously.
Evidence identification links asynchronous queries to relevant historical observations and response triggers.

New stream observations are continuously appended under a fixed retention procedure. For AViLA, this specifically supports fixed-rule insertion or replacement of comprehensive streaming observation memory.
Temporal evidence links are updated as asynchronous support arrives. For AViLA, this specifically supports relinking or reindexing of stored items of comprehensive streaming observation memory.

derived.hybrid_relation: Distinct operative representation paths are explicitly linked for downstream retrieval, reasoning, or control.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 6): During inference, the operative memory component (comprehensive streaming observation memory) changes through fixed-rule insertion or replacement, relinking or reindexing of stored items; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
